summary.headline: Patel Engineering Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue flat at INR 1211 crore; H1 PAT up 15.94% to INR 177 crore, FY27 growth guided to 7-8%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue was INR 1211 crore versus INR 1208 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA margin down to 12.42% from 13.13% and PAT up 7.64% to INR 83 crore. Management blamed uneven monsoon rain in hilly project sites and delayed new project starts pending forest clearances. Order book stood at INR 13,546 crore at September 30, 2026, and bids worth about INR 30,000 crore are pending, with management expecting most to open by March. Management cut its FY27 revenue growth expectation to roughly 7-8% from the earlier 10%, with stronger growth deferred to FY28.

segments.name: Hydropower
segments.commentary: Hydropower is 64% of order book and 71% of standalone Q2 revenue. Subansiri: Unit 5 commissioned, five of eight units (1250 MW) now on grid, remaining three targeted within FY27.

segments.name: Irrigation
segments.commentary: Irrigation is 14% of order book and 14% of standalone Q2 revenue. Sleemanabad irrigation project achieved breakthrough of a ~12 km tunnel, described as India's longest irrigation tunnel, and is moving to final completion.

segments.name: Tunnelling
segments.commentary: Tunnelling is 4% of order book and 11% of standalone Q2 revenue. Company says it owns four TBMs.

segments.name: Roads, urban infrastructure and others
segments.commentary: Accounts for 18% of order book and 4% of standalone Q2 revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth now expected at roughly 7-8% (marginal), down from the earlier 10% guidance; management said H2 will not be sufficient to hit 10%.
FY28 growth expected to pick up as new projects from the ~INR 30,000 crore bid pipeline mobilise; 6-7 month mobilisation phase cited before revenue ramps.
FY29 and beyond: earlier 15-20% growth ambition was referenced by an analyst; management declined to commit beyond FY28 visibility.
Arbitration awards: on track for INR 100-150 crore in FY27; INR 80 crore already received in H1 with balance expected by March via awards or land sales.
Capex about 3% of new project value, funded from client advances; analyst-cited run-rate of about INR 150 crore per year for FY27-FY29 was confirmed by management.
No dividend or distribution planned for FY27; capital needed for new project wins. Dividend review deferred to next year.
capex_capacity: Subansiri (8 units): 5 units operational, 1250 MW supplied to grid; remaining 3 units on track for completion within FY27.
Kwar (J&K): over 4 lakh cubic metres of dam concreting done against ~7.5 lakh cubic metres; TRT outlet bridge completed; powerhouse excavation complete, concreting underway.
Kiru (J&K): ~12 lakh cubic metres of dam concreting done against 12.5 lakh cubic metres required; powerhouse slab concreting up to service floor completed for all four units.
Shongtong (Himachal Pradesh): concreting progressing steadily; no quantitative update given.
Capex: heavy machinery such as TBMs bought for multi-project use; dumpers and moving equipment leased. Annual capex flagged at around INR 150 crore per year for FY27-FY29 in the Q&A.
demand_pricing: Order book INR 13,546 crore at September 30, 2026, mix hydropower 64%, irrigation 14%, tunnelling 4%, roads/urban/others 18%.

Bids submitted worth ~INR 30,000 crore across ~15 projects, including Dorjilung 1125 MW (Bhutan), THDC Kalai-II 1200 MW, NHPC Kamala 1720 MW (Arunachal Pradesh), Sawalkote 1856 MW (J&K), and private pumped storage projects. Bidding was about INR 8,000-9,000 crore around June 2026.

Management expects a further ~INR 50,000 crore of projects to come up for bidding over the next 12 months, including Ladakh/J&K roads and tunnels, railway, Maharashtra/MP/AP pumped storage and hydro projects.

Hydro competition: management says four to five bidders in large hydro, less competition than other sectors. Company says it has the PQ to bid any size or type of project in hydro, irrigation and tunnelling.

Order award timing: management expects the bulk of the ~INR 30,000 crore to open by March 2026 and LOIs possibly in Q4. In the prior year INR 4,400 crore inflow was reported, with only ~INR 700 crore in hydro; a ~INR 14,000-15,000 crore Dibang project went to a new entrant.
Pass-through: most projects have price escalation clauses, though realisation can lag due to calculation timing. Margin dip attributed to monsoon, early-stage mobilisation work, and cost inflation.
Receivable days: management said the H1 receivables spike is timing-related and expects to return to the 40-45 to 50 day range. Working capital lines are reassessed annually.

qa_highlights.question: Is H2 revenue likely to pick up enough to hit the 10% FY27 growth guidance, and what about FY28-29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 growth will be marginal, around 7-8%. FY28 is expected to pick up as the ~INR 30,000 crore bids open and mobilise after a 6-7 month phase; FY28 visibility is limited.

qa_highlights.question: How much hydropower did the industry win in the last six months, and what did the company win in the prior year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no hydro projects were finalised in the last six months. Last year's INR 4,400 crore inflow included about INR 700 crore of hydro, with one project won out of three or four bids.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company buy back shares, or pay dividends given free cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: No dividend or distribution is planned this year because capital is needed for bids that may open. Management will review next year. A buyback was not addressed beyond 'will discuss internally'.

qa_highlights.question: Will the land bank be monetised to cut debt and release pledged shares?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said land sales are ongoing but depend on market conditions. Over the last four to five years more than INR 1000 crore of land was sold. Promoter pledge fell from about 88-90% to 67%, and further reduction was pushed to next year.

qa_highlights.question: Will total debt rise as new projects are won?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital debt will rise with new projects, but management expects land sales and award receipts to offset this on a year-on-year basis. Some intra-year increase is possible.

qa_highlights.question: What is the TBM supply risk from China, and what about cost inflation and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Company owns four TBMs and can source from Germany or India if needed. Most projects have escalation clauses, with some lag in realisation. Margin dip attributed to monsoon, mobilisation-phase work and cost inflation.

risks_watch: Revenue growth guidance cut to 7-8% for FY27; the 10% target is no longer expected.
Bid conversion: ~INR 30,000 crore pending, with management expecting most to open by March 2026; delays in forest clearances have already deferred project starts.
Promoter pledge at 67% (down from ~88-90%); promoter stake reduced from ~39% to ~31%, and promoters did not take up the rights issue. Management gave no timeline for pledge reduction beyond FY28.
Debt rose to INR 1312 crore from INR 1187 crore in March, with working capital debt INR 960 crore; receivables spiked in H1, which management attributes to milestone-payment timing.
Arbitration award realisation (INR 100-150 crore target) and land monetisation are not in management's control and carry timing risk.
China export restrictions on TBMs; the company has four TBMs owned and alternatives sourced from Germany or India.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term hydro and tunnelling pipeline, but cautious and vague on near-term revenue and on non-core asset and land-sale specifics, where answers were brief and some analyst questions were deferred. Management conceded the FY27 growth cut and gave hedged replies on pledge reduction, buyback and dividends.
key_quotes: The monsoon this year was somewhat uneven. While overall rainfall remained below normal, certain project locations, particularly in the hilly regions, experienced spells of heavy rainfall resulting in temporary disruptions to construction activities.
So, we see, we are fairly confident we will get our share of work.
Yes, we see the majority might open by March, correct.
So, as a combination on a year -on-year basis, we do not see a substantial increase in debt. But in between, it can happen that some debt goes up.
We will discuss internally. Thank you.
